subject: [PATCH v5 02/11] mm: add PMD swap entry splitting support

2026-07-22.patch_summary: This patch adds support for splitting a PMD swap entry into 512 PTE swap entries in the Linux kernel's memory management (mm) module. The patch introduces a new branch in the __split_huge_pmd_locked() function that handles PMD swap entries, which are used to represent large blocks of swap space. Unlike migration splits, no folio reference is needed for swap entries because they point to swap slots rather than pages. The patch also includes changes to handle the case where a present THP split has already cleared the pmd, and adds warnings to catch any future callers that break an invariant related to the freeze path.

reviews.author: Dev Jain
reviews.summary:
The reviewer pointed out that the patch's wording is confusing, specifically stating that swap entries require a reference to swap slots, not folios, and suggested removing the mention of migration.

Reviewer Dev Jain suggested that the for loops in the patch could be improved by using a set_softleaf_ptes() helper function, providing a link to an existing implementation
reviews.raw_body:
Confusing wording. swap entries need reference of swap slots instead
of folios. I would drop the mention of migration here.

2026-07-24.patch_summary: This patch adds support for splitting a PMD swap entry into 512 PTE swap entries in the Linux kernel's memory management (mm) module. The patch addresses the issue of handling PMD swap entries, which are used to represent large blocks of swap space, by introducing a new branch in the __split_huge_pmd_locked function that splits these entries into smaller PTEs. This allows for more efficient use of swap space and improves the overall performance of the system. The patch also includes additional checks and handling for cases where the PMD is not present or has been invalidated, ensuring that the system remains stable even in these scenarios.
